verdict.rationale: Pigment documents an official MCP server that lets external agents such as Claude, Cursor and Codex build and edit Pigment models. Its sessions are authenticated through enterprise identity, and the product keeps detailed edit histories down to the data block level, plus an Audit Trail API for application events. However, nothing in the evidence explicitly says that agent-made changes land in the same audit trail as human edits, or that forecast and scenario edits specifically are supported through this interface. missing for 10: explicit documentation that MCP/agent edits are recorded and attributed in the same audit history as human edits, documented scenario/forecast write operations via the machine interface, a published API/tool schema (OpenAPI probes returned 404), independent or hands-on corroboration

support.subject: As an AI-native user, an agent can build or update a forecast or scenario through a documented machine interface, and the change lands in the same audit trail as a human edit

citations.quote: Build and edit your Pigment model directly from tools like Claude, Cursor, and Codex, without switching interfaces.
Every session is authenticated through enterprise identity, and access is scoped by role, model, or metric.
your applications each have detailed histories down to the data block level, which offer full visibility into the edit events
With the Audit Trail API, you can ingest login, administration, security and application events into your SIEM
